docs.title: Z-Wave
docs.text: A node reported dead has stopped answering the controller. Battery devices sleep and legitimately show as unavailable until their next wake-up, which can be hours. For mains-powered nodes, a dead status usually means the device lost power or drifted out of mesh range. Wake the device manually, then run Rebuild Routes on that single node. Do not rebuild routes for the whole network unless several nodes are affected, as it saturates the mesh for a long time.

docs.title: ESPHome
docs.text: An ESPHome node showing unavailable has lost its API connection. Check Wi-Fi signal strength on the node's diagnostic sensors — anything below -80 dBm is marginal. Nodes reboot-loop when a component fails to initialise; the serial log from the ESPHome add-on shows the failing component. A node that is powered but unreachable often has a static IP colliding with a DHCP lease.

docs.title: Home Assistant Core
docs.text: `unavailable` means the integration cannot reach the device; `unknown` means it is reachable but has not reported a value yet. A whole integration going unavailable at once points at the hub, bridge or broker rather than the individual devices. Check Settings > Devices & Services for a config entry showing "Failed to set up", and read the error in Settings > System > Logs.

RELEVANT DOCS:
  [zwave_js-troubleshooting] Z-Wave — Node is dead or unavailable
      A node reported dead has stopped answering the controller. Battery devices sleep and legitimately show as unavailable until their next wake-up, which can be hours. For mains-powered nodes, a dead status usually means the device lost power or drifted out of mesh range. Wake the device manually, then run Rebuild Routes on that single node. Do not rebuild routes for the whole network unless several nodes are affected, as it saturates the mesh for a long time.
  [esphome-troubleshooting] ESPHome — Node offline or unavailable
      An ESPHome node showing unavailable has lost its API connection. Check Wi-Fi signal strength on the node's diagnostic sensors — anything below -80 dBm is marginal. Nodes reboot-loop when a component fails to initialise; the serial log from the ESPHome add-on shows the failing component. A node that is powered but unreachable often has a static IP colliding with a DHCP lease.
  [homeassistant-troubleshooting] Home Assistant Core — Entity unavailable or unknown
      `unavailable` means the integration cannot reach the device; `unknown` means it is reachable but has not reported a value yet. A whole integration going unavailable at once points at the hub, bridge or broker rather than the individual devices. Check Settings > Devices & Services for a config entry showing "Failed to set up", and read the error in Settings > System > Logs.
